AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 (monster stream), copied verbatim per governing rule 3 and not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (queen.py:47-51). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire. sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion -- the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering -- MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) *before* the subclass applies its powers, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: this unit's initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power that listens on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7: the four relic files and powers.py cited above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py IS hashed here for other entries); flagged explicitly as the shared finding instructs. ESCALATION CHECK: TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:40-44 applies MinionPower 1m to itself and nothing else. MinionPower is a marker with no AfterApplied and no amount arithmetic (MinionPower.cs: Type Buff, StackType Single, ShouldPlayVfx false, OwnerIsSecondaryEnemy true, ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath false, ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal false), so the apply-time inversions the shared finding describes cannot reach it: it reads no HP, no combat.enemies and no hook result. C# passes `base.Creature` as applier and the sim omits it; MinionPower reads no applier on either side. Clause (c) holds -- the initial state is the MoveState TACKLE_MOVE, so the constructor roll is a sticky no-op.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:46-65. FIVE MoveStates with matching ids -- and this is the detail a hasty port loses: TACKLE_MOVE and TACKLE_2_MOVE are SEPARATE states sharing one TackleMove delegate, and TACKLE_3_MOVE / TACKLE_4_MOVE are likewise two states sharing WeakTackleMove, which is exactly what queen.py:54-71 builds (two MoveStates both bound to self._tackle, two both bound to self._weak_tackle). Distinct ids matter because the machine keys its state dict by id (monster_state_machine step 3 / G8 clause a); collapsing either pair would shorten the cycle. Chain matches: TACKLE -> TACKLE_2 -> BEAM -> TACKLE_3 -> TACKLE_4 -> BEAM (TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:54-58 vs queen.py:72-76), i.e. a two-move prologue into a three-move loop, with INITIAL state TACKLE_MOVE (:64 vs :77). No branch state, so no AddBranch integer and no MonsterAi draw. Intents match: SingleAttackIntent(18) x2 -> ATTACK 18; MultiAttackIntent(8, 3) -> ATTACK damage=8 hits=3; SingleAttackIntent(14) x2 -> ATTACK 14.

guards.what: Encounter order: the amalgam must exist before the Queen is added
guards.rationale: Queen.AfterAddedToRoom does `Enemies.First(c => c.Monster is TorchHeadAmalgam)` (Queen.cs:128), which throws unless the amalgam is already in Enemies -- so the C# boss adds the amalgam first. The sim's QUEEN_BOSS lists monster_classes=[TorchHeadAmalgam, Queen] (queen.py:194-197) in that order, and combat.py:240-244 constructs them in list order, so net_ids and the enemy-list order agree with the source. 'queen' is in Glory's boss_keys (rooms.py).
